**Surah al-Hashr is Madani.** [[Al-Dhahhak ibn Mazahim, Ibn al-Dharis, al-Nahhas, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that he said: "Surah al-Hashr was revealed in Madinah." Ibn Mardawayh narrated a similar report from Ibn al-Zubayr. See al-Durr al-Manthur (al-Suyuti): 8/88.]]

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: I said to Ibn Abbas, "Surat al-Hashr?" He said, "Say: Surat al-Nadir." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the Book of Tafsir, Surat al-Hashr: 8/629.]]

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ The commentators said: This surah was revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir. [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in the place cited above, and by Muslim in the Book of Tafsir, chapter on Surat Bara'ah, al-Anfal and al-Hashr, no. (3031): 4/2322, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr.]] The reason was that the Prophet ﷺ entered Madinah, and the Banu al-Nadir made a treaty with him that they would not fight him nor fight alongside him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ accepted this from them. When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ conducted the battle of Badr and prevailed over the polytheists, the Banu al-Nadir said: "By Allah, he is truly the Prophet whose description we found in the Torah; his banner will not be turned back." But when he fought at Uhud and the Muslims were defeated, they became doubtful, showed enmity toward the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and the believers, and broke the covenant that existed between them and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf rode with forty Jewish riders to Makkah. They came to the Quraysh, made alliances with them, and agreed that their word would be one against Muhammad ﷺ. Abu Sufyan entered al-Masjid al-Haram with forty men, and Ka'b with forty Jews, and they took a pledge from one another between the curtains and the Ka'bah. Then Ka'b and his companions returned to Madinah. Jibril descended and informed the Prophet ﷺ of what Ka'b and Abu Sufyan had agreed upon. The Prophet ﷺ then ordered the killing of Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf, and Muhammad ibn Maslamah killed him. [[We have mentioned this in Surat Al 'Imran. See above: 2/147.]]

The Prophet ﷺ had discovered treachery from them when he came to them regarding the blood money of the two Muslim men whom Amr ibn Umayyah al-Damri had killed on his return from Bi'r Ma'unah. They resolved to drop a stone on him from above the fortress, but Allah protected him and informed him of that. [[We have mentioned this in Surat al-Ma'idah. See above: 3/28.]]

When Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf was killed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ rose in the morning and ordered the people to march against the Banu al-Nadir, who were in a village called Zuhrah. When the Prophet ﷺ marched toward them, he found them wailing over Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. They said, "O Muhammad, a wailing after a wailing and a weeping after a weeping?" He said, "Yes." They said, "Leave us to weep for our grief, then decide your matter." The Prophet ﷺ said, "Leave Madinah." They said, "Death is nearer to us than that." Then they called to war and announced fighting. The hypocrites, Abdullah ibn Ubayy and his companions, sent secretly to them: "Do not leave the fortress. If they fight you, we are with you and will not abandon you; we will surely help you, and if you are expelled, we will surely go out with you." So they fortified the alleys and barricaded them. Then they agreed to betray the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and sent to him: "Come out with thirty men of your companions, and thirty of us will come out, so that we may meet at a place between us and you, and they will listen to you. If they believe you and have faith in you, we will all believe." The Prophet ﷺ went out with thirty of his companions, and thirty Jewish scholars came out to him. When they reached an open place, some of the Jews said to others, "How can you reach him while thirty men of his companions are with him, all of whom wish to die before him?" Then they sent to him: "How can we understand when we are sixty men? Come out with three of your companions, and we will come out to you with three of our scholars. They will listen to you, and if they believe in you, we will all believe in you and affirm you." So the Prophet ﷺ went out with three of his companions, and three of the Jews came out, concealing daggers, intending to assassinate the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. A sincere woman from the Banu al-Nadir sent to her brother, who was a Muslim man of the Ansar, and informed him of what the Banu al-Nadir intended of treachery against the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Her brother hurried until he reached the Prophet ﷺ and told him their news secretly before the Prophet ﷺ reached them. The Prophet ﷺ returned. The next day, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out to them with the battalions and besieged them for twenty-one nights. Allah cast terror into their hearts and they despaired of the support of the hypocrites. They asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for peace, but he refused except that they leave Madinah according to what the Prophet ﷺ ordered them. They accepted this. He made peace with them on the condition of exile, and that they would have what their camels could carry of their property, except the weapons, which is the *halqah*, and that they would leave to them their homes, their land, and all their other property. [[Abu Dawud narrated part of it in the Book of Kharaj and Imarah, chapter on the report about the Nadir: 4/234–235. Abd al-Razzaq narrated it at length in al-Musannaf: 5/359–360, and al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr 8/93 also to Abd ibn Humayd and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il. See also Tafsir Ibn Kathir: 4/331–332.]]

Ibn Abbas said: On condition that every household of three tents would load one camel with whatever goods they wished, and the Prophet of Allah ﷺ would have what remained.

al-Dahhak said: Every three persons were given a camel and a water-skin, and they did so and left Madinah for Syria, to Adhri'at and Ariha, except two households from among them, the family of Abu al-Huqayq and the family of Huyayy ibn Akhtab, who joined Khaybar. A group of them joined al-Hirah. [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/31–32. Al-Suyuti attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur 8/91 also to Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il.]] This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He:

﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture...﴾

**Al-Baghawi's commentary (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 59, verse 2:**

﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book﴾, meaning the Banu al-Nadir, ﴿from their homes﴾, which were in Yathrib. Ibn Ishaq said: The expulsion of the Banu al-Nadir took place after the Prophet (ﷺ) returned from Uhud, and the conquest of Quraydhah took place when he returned from the Confederates (al-Ahzab), and between the two there were two years.

﴿At the first gathering﴾. Al-Zuhri said: They were from a tribe that had not been struck by expulsion in the past, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had decreed expulsion upon them, and had it not been for that, He would have punished them in this world. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/28.]

Ibn Abbas said: Whoever doubts that the gathering place is in al-Sham (Greater Syria), let him recite this verse. This was the first gathering to al-Sham. The Prophet (ﷺ) said to them: "Go out." They said: "To where?" He said: "To the land of the gathering. Then creation will be gathered on the Day of Resurrection to al-Sham." [See: Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir: 4/333; al-Qurtubi: 18/2.]

Al-Kalbi said: He only said "at the first gathering" because they were the first of the People of the Book to be expelled from the Arabian Peninsula. Then their last (group) was expelled by Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him.

Murrah al-Hamdani said: The first gathering was from Madinah, and the second gathering was from Khaybar and the whole Arabian Peninsula to Adhri'at and Ariha in al-Sham, in the days of Umar.

Qatadah said: This was the first gathering, and the second gathering is a fire that will gather them from the east to the west; it will spend the night with them wherever they spend the night, and it will rest with them wherever they rest. [See: al-Tabari: 28/29.]

﴿You did not think﴾, O believers, ﴿that they would leave﴾ Madinah, ﴿because of their might and their strength. That was because they were people of fortresses, property, and many palm trees.

﴿And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from Allah﴾. That is: the Banu al-Nadir thought that their fortresses would protect them from the authority of Allah. ﴿But Allah came upon them﴾, that is, the command of Allah and His punishment, ﴿from where they did not expect﴾, namely that He commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to fight them and expel them, and they did not suspect this. ﴿And He cast terror into their hearts﴾ by the killing of their chief, Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf.

﴿They destroy﴾: Abu Amr recited it with the shaddah (intensive form, يُخَرِّبُونَ), while the others recited it without (يُخْرِبُونَ). Both readings have the same meaning. ﴿Their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers﴾. Al-Zuhri said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) made a settlement with them that they could take whatever the camels could carry, they would look at the wood in their dwellings, tear it down, pull out whatever they found good, and load it onto their camels, while the believers would destroy what remained. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/29–30.] Ibn Zayd said: They would uproot the pillars, break down the roofs, dig through the walls, and pull out the wood, even the tent pegs, destroying them so that the believers would not live in them, out of envy and hatred. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/29–30.] Qatadah said: The Muslims would destroy what was adjacent to them from the outside, and the Jews would destroy it from the inside. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/29.]

Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: Whenever the Muslims gained control over one of their houses, they would demolish it so that the battle space would be wider for them. The enemies of Allah would dig through their houses from behind, exit into the next one, and fortify themselves there, breaking what was in front of them, and they would throw at the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) from the house they had exited. This is the meaning of His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿They destroy their houses by their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning﴾, that is, take admonition and reflect on what befell them, ﴿O you who have vision﴾, that is, O you who have intellect and insight.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verse 3:

﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾, meaning the departure from their homeland, ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾ with killing and captivity, as He did with the Banu Qurayzah. ﴿And for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.﴾

﴿Dhalika﴾ (That), which befell them, ﴿because they opposed God and His Messenger. And whoever opposes God, indeed God is severe in punishment﴾.

﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾ [59:5], the verse. The reason is that when the Messenger of God (ﷺ) descended upon Banu al-Nadir and they took refuge in their fortresses, he ordered that their palm trees be cut down and burned. The enemies of God were distressed by this and said: "O Muhammad, you claimed that you desired reform! Is it reform to hack down trees and cut palm trees? Have you found corruption on earth in what you claimed was revealed to you?" The Muslims were troubled within themselves by their words and feared that this would be corruption. They disagreed about it. Some of them said: "Do not cut them, for it is part of what God granted us as fay' (spoils returned without battle)." Others said: "Rather, we will infuriate them by cutting them." So God revealed this verse, confirming those who forbade cutting and absolving those who cut of sin.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi related to us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il (al-Bukhari) related to us, Adam related to us, al-Layth related to us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) burned the palm trees of Banu al-Nadir and cut down al-Buwayra, and then (the verse) was revealed: ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of God﴾ [59:5].[[Related by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, Tafsir of Surat al-Hashr, chapter "Whatever palm trees you cut down": 8/629, and Muslim in Jihad, chapter on the permissibility of cutting the trees of unbelievers, no. 1746: 3/1365–1366.]]

﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of God﴾: God informs in this verse that whatever they cut and whatever they left was by the permission of God, ﴿and that He might disgrace the defiantly disobedient﴾ [59:5].

They differed concerning the word "lina" (a type of palm). A group said: all palm trees are lina except the ajwa (a prized date variety). This is the view of Ikrimah and Qatadah,[[al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur (8/98) attributes Ikrimah's view to Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shayba, Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir, and Qatadah's view in the same place to Abd ibn Humayd.]] and Zadhan related it from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Prophet (ﷺ) used to cut their palm trees except the ajwa.[[The words between the brackets are missing from manuscript "A".]] The people of Medina call all dates other than the ajwa "al-alwan" (the colors), its singular being "laun" and "lina." Al-Zuhri said: they are all the colors of palm trees except the ajwa and the barniyya.

Mujahid and Ata said: they are all palm trees without exception. Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both: it is a variety of palm tree. Sufyan said: they are the noble palm trees.

Muqatil said: it is a kind of palm tree whose fruit is called "al-laun," which is very yellow, its pit visible from the outside, and in which a molar tooth is lost (i.e., it is so soft it sinks in when chewed). It was among their finest dates and the most desirable to them. A single palm of it was worth the price of a wasif (a young male servant), and it was dearer to them than a wasif. When they saw them cutting it down, this grieved them, and they said to the believers: "You dislike corruption on earth, yet you are corrupting! Leave this palm standing; it belongs to whoever prevails over it." So God Most High informed that this was by His permission.[[In manuscript "A" (the text reads): "Indeed it is the price of whoever prevails over it."]] [158/a]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verses 6–7:

﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger﴾, meaning He returned it to His Messenger. It is said: *afa'a yafi'u*, meaning "he returned." And Allah restored it ﴿from them﴾, meaning from the Jews of Banu al-Nadir. ﴿You did not spur toward it﴾, meaning you did not urge your mounts toward it, ﴿with horses or riding camels﴾. It is said: *wajafa al-faras wa al-ba'ir yajifu wajifan*, which means rapid travel, and *awjafahu sahibuhu* means that its rider drove it to travel quickly. By *rikab* he means the camels that carry people. This is because when Banu al-Nadir abandoned their estates and their lands, the Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divide them among them, as he had done with the spoils of Khaybar. Allah the Exalted then made clear in this verse that it is *fay'* (spoils obtained without battle), which the Muslims did not obtain by means of horses or riding camels, did not travel any distance to reach, did not suffer hardship for, and did not face in battle. ﴿But Allah gives power to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. So Allah made the wealth of Banu al-Nadir exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to place it wherever he wished. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) distributed it among the Muhajirun (Emigrants), and he gave nothing from it to the Ansar (Helpers) except three men who were in need: Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, Sahl ibn Hunayf, and al-Harith ibn al-Simmah [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, page 166: "al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain of narration."]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan al-Nadri informed me that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) summoned him when his chamberlain Yarfa' came to him and said: "Would you be willing to see Uthman, Abd al-Rahman, al-Zubayr and Sa'd, who are asking permission to enter?" He said: "Yes," so he admitted them. Yarfa' waited a little, then came back and said: "Would you be willing to see Abbas and Ali, who are asking permission?" He said: "Yes." When the two entered, Abbas said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this man," while they were disputing over what Allah had restored to His Messenger from Banu al-Nadir. The group said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve one of them from the other." He said: "Be patient. I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity,' meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself?" They said: "He did say that." Then Umar turned to Ali and Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "I will tell you about this matter. Allah had specially granted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) something from the *fay'* that He had given to no one else. He said: 'And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur toward it any horses or riding camels,' up to His words, 'competent.' This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He did not withhold it from you, nor did he monopolize it over you. He gave it to you and distributed it among you until this wealth remained from it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would spend on his family their yearly provision from this wealth, then take what remained and place it in the position of Allah's wealth. He acted in this way throughout his life. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) died, and Abu Bakr said: 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So Abu Bakr took possession of it and acted with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had acted with it, and you were all present at that time." Then he turned to Ali and Abbas and said: "You two claim that Abu Bakr did with it what you say, and Allah knows that in this matter he was truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then Allah took Abu Bakr, and I said: 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of Abu Bakr,' and I took possession of it for two years of my caliphate, acting with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had acted and as Abu Bakr had acted. Allah knows that in this matter I am truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then you both came to me, and your word was one and your matter was the same. I said to you both: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity.' When it appeared best to me to hand it over to you, I said: 'If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you both give Allah's covenant and His pledge that you will act with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr acted, and as I have acted with it since I took charge of it. Otherwise, do not speak to me about it.' You said: 'Hand it over to us on those terms,' so I handed it over to you. Do you now seek from me a judgment other than that? By Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand, I will not judge it otherwise until the Hour is established. If you are unable to manage it, then return it to me, for I will suffice you in it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Fara'id*, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity": 12/6, and in *al-Maghazi*: 7/334–335; and Muslim in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the ruling on *fay'*, no. (1757): 3/1377–1379.]].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, meaning from the wealth of the unbelieving people of the towns. Ibn Abbas said: they are Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Fadak, Khaybar, and the villages of Uraynah. ﴿Belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler﴾. We have mentioned in the commentary on surah al-Anfal the ruling on *ghanimah* (war booty) and the ruling on *fay'*. The wealth of *fay'* belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime; he would place it wherever he wished, spend from it on his family their yearly provision, and place what remained in the position of Allah's wealth [[See above: 3/361.]].

Scholars differed about the disbursement of *fay'* after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One group said it belongs to the imams after him.

Al-Shafi'i had two opinions on it: the first is that it belongs to the fighters, and the second is that it is for the interests of the Muslims. One begins with the fighters, then with the most important of the interests, in order of importance.

They differed concerning the division of *fay'* wealth into fifths. Some held that it is divided into five, with one fifth going to the people of *ghanimah* and four fifths to the fighters and the public interests. Most scholars held that it is not divided into fifths, but that the disbursement of all of it is one and the same, and all Muslims have a right in it. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, and those who came after them﴾, and then said: "This has encompassed the Muslims in general." He also said: "There is no Muslim on the face of the earth who does not have a right in this *fay'*, except what your right hands possess" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Imarah*, chapter on recording the stipends: 4/214, and al-Mundhiri said: "This is *munqati'* (disconnected), as al-Zuhri did not hear from Umar." Also al-Bayhaqi in *al-Sunan*: 6/347–352. Parts of it were narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in *al-Tafsir*: 2/284, Abu Ubayd in *al-Amwal*: pp. 243–244, and al-Tabari: 28/37. Al-Albani authenticated it as *mawquf* (ending with Umar). See *Irwa' al-Ghalil*: 5/83–84.]].

﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity among the rich among you﴾. The majority recited it with the *ya'* (*yakuna*), with *dawlatan* in the accusative, meaning "so that the *fay'* does not become a circulating commodity." Abu Ja'far recited *takuna* with the *ta'*, and *dawlatun* in the nominative as the subject of *kana*, meaning: "so that the matter does not come to a *dawlah* (a turn of fortune)," treating *al-kaynunah* as meaning "occurrence," and in that case it has no predicate. *Al-dawlah* is the name for that which people pass around among themselves. ﴿Among the rich among you﴾, meaning among the leaders and the powerful, who would then dominate the poor and the weak with it. This is because in the pre-Islamic period, when they seized booty, the chief would take a quarter of it for himself, which was called *al-mirba'*, and then he would choose whatever he wished from it after the *mirba'*. Allah made this belong to His Messenger (ﷺ), to divide it as he was commanded. Then He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾, meaning what he gives you, ﴿gives you﴾ [from the *fay'* and the *ghanimah*] [[What is between the parentheses is missing from "a"]], ﴿take it, and whatever he forbids you﴾ from misappropriation and other things, ﴿refrain from it﴾. This was revealed concerning the wealth of *fay'*, but it is general for everything the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded and forbade.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair, and the women who file their teeth for beauty, who alter Allah's creation." News of this reached a woman from Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, so she came and said: "It has reached me that you cursed such-and-such." He said: "Why should I not curse one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and who is in the Book of Allah, the Exalted?" She said: "I have read everything between the two covers and did not find in it what you say." He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it. Did you not read: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]?" She said: "Yes." He said: "He has indeed forbidden it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Tafsir*, surah al-Hashr, chapter on ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾: 8/630, and Muslim in *al-Libas*, chapter on the prohibition of the *wasilah* and the *mustawsilah* act, no. (2125): 3/1678.]]. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Then he explained who has the right to the *fay'*, saying: ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verses 6–7:

﴿And what Allah restored to His Messenger﴾, meaning He returned it to His Messenger. It is said: *afa'a yafi'u*, meaning "he returned." And Allah restored it ﴿from them﴾, meaning from the Jews of Banu al-Nadir. ﴿You did not spur toward it﴾, meaning you did not urge your mounts toward it, ﴿with horses or riding camels﴾. It is said: *wajafa al-faras wa al-ba'ir yajifu wajifan*, which means rapid travel, and *awjafahu sahibuhu* means that its rider drove it to travel quickly. By *rikab* he means the camels that carry people. This is because when Banu al-Nadir abandoned their estates and their lands, the Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) to divide them among them, as he had done with the spoils of Khaybar. Allah the Exalted then made clear in this verse that it is *fay'* (spoils obtained without battle), which the Muslims did not obtain by means of horses or riding camels, did not travel any distance to reach, did not suffer hardship for, and did not face in battle. ﴿But Allah gives power to His messengers over whomever He wills, and Allah is over all things competent﴾. So Allah made the wealth of Banu al-Nadir exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), to place it wherever he wished. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) distributed it among the Muhajirun (Emigrants), and he gave nothing from it to the Ansar (Helpers) except three men who were in need: Abu Dujanah Simak ibn Kharashah, Sahl ibn Hunayf, and al-Harith ibn al-Simmah [[Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shafi, page 166: "al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain of narration."]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abu al-Yaman narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri, who said: Malik ibn Aws ibn al-Hadathan al-Nadri informed me that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) summoned him when his chamberlain Yarfa' came to him and said: "Would you be willing to see Uthman, Abd al-Rahman, al-Zubayr and Sa'd, who are asking permission to enter?" He said: "Yes," so he admitted them. Yarfa' waited a little, then came back and said: "Would you be willing to see Abbas and Ali, who are asking permission?" He said: "Yes." When the two entered, Abbas said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between me and this man," while they were disputing over what Allah had restored to His Messenger from Banu al-Nadir. The group said: "O Commander of the Faithful, judge between them and relieve one of them from the other." He said: "Be patient. I adjure you by Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity,' meaning the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) himself?" They said: "He did say that." Then Umar turned to Ali and Abbas and said: "I adjure you both by Allah: do you know that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said that?" They said: "Yes." He said: "I will tell you about this matter. Allah had specially granted the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) something from the *fay'* that He had given to no one else. He said: 'And what Allah restored to His Messenger from them, you did not spur toward it any horses or riding camels,' up to His words, 'competent.' This was exclusively for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He did not withhold it from you, nor did he monopolize it over you. He gave it to you and distributed it among you until this wealth remained from it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would spend on his family their yearly provision from this wealth, then take what remained and place it in the position of Allah's wealth. He acted in this way throughout his life. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) died, and Abu Bakr said: 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ).' So Abu Bakr took possession of it and acted with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had acted with it, and you were all present at that time." Then he turned to Ali and Abbas and said: "You two claim that Abu Bakr did with it what you say, and Allah knows that in this matter he was truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then Allah took Abu Bakr, and I said: 'I am the guardian of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and of Abu Bakr,' and I took possession of it for two years of my caliphate, acting with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had acted and as Abu Bakr had acted. Allah knows that in this matter I am truthful, righteous, rightly guided, and a follower of the truth. Then you both came to me, and your word was one and your matter was the same. I said to you both: 'The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity.' When it appeared best to me to hand it over to you, I said: 'If you wish, I will hand it over to you on the condition that you both give Allah's covenant and His pledge that you will act with it as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr acted, and as I have acted with it since I took charge of it. Otherwise, do not speak to me about it.' You said: 'Hand it over to us on those terms,' so I handed it over to you. Do you now seek from me a judgment other than that? By Allah, by whose leave the heavens and the earth stand, I will not judge it otherwise until the Hour is established. If you are unable to manage it, then return it to me, for I will suffice you in it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Fara'id*, chapter on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ) "We do not leave inheritance; what we leave is charity": 12/6, and in *al-Maghazi*: 7/334–335; and Muslim in *al-Jihad*, chapter on the ruling on *fay'*, no. (1757): 3/1377–1379.]].

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾, meaning from the wealth of the unbelieving people of the towns. Ibn Abbas said: they are Qurayzah, al-Nadir, Fadak, Khaybar, and the villages of Uraynah. ﴿Belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler﴾. We have mentioned in the commentary on surah al-Anfal the ruling on *ghanimah* (war booty) and the ruling on *fay'*. The wealth of *fay'* belonged to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime; he would place it wherever he wished, spend from it on his family their yearly provision, and place what remained in the position of Allah's wealth [[See above: 3/361.]].

Scholars differed about the disbursement of *fay'* after the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). One group said it belongs to the imams after him.

Al-Shafi'i had two opinions on it: the first is that it belongs to the fighters, and the second is that it is for the interests of the Muslims. One begins with the fighters, then with the most important of the interests, in order of importance.

They differed concerning the division of *fay'* wealth into fifths. Some held that it is divided into five, with one fifth going to the people of *ghanimah* and four fifths to the fighters and the public interests. Most scholars held that it is not divided into fifths, but that the disbursement of all of it is one and the same, and all Muslims have a right in it. Umar ibn al-Khattab recited: ﴿What Allah restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ until he reached ﴿for the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, and those who came after them﴾, and then said: "This has encompassed the Muslims in general." He also said: "There is no Muslim on the face of the earth who does not have a right in this *fay'*, except what your right hands possess" [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in *al-Imarah*, chapter on recording the stipends: 4/214, and al-Mundhiri said: "This is *munqati'* (disconnected), as al-Zuhri did not hear from Umar." Also al-Bayhaqi in *al-Sunan*: 6/347–352. Parts of it were narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in *al-Tafsir*: 2/284, Abu Ubayd in *al-Amwal*: pp. 243–244, and al-Tabari: 28/37. Al-Albani authenticated it as *mawquf* (ending with Umar). See *Irwa' al-Ghalil*: 5/83–84.]].

﴿So that it does not become a circulating commodity among the rich among you﴾. The majority recited it with the *ya'* (*yakuna*), with *dawlatan* in the accusative, meaning "so that the *fay'* does not become a circulating commodity." Abu Ja'far recited *takuna* with the *ta'*, and *dawlatun* in the nominative as the subject of *kana*, meaning: "so that the matter does not come to a *dawlah* (a turn of fortune)," treating *al-kaynunah* as meaning "occurrence," and in that case it has no predicate. *Al-dawlah* is the name for that which people pass around among themselves. ﴿Among the rich among you﴾, meaning among the leaders and the powerful, who would then dominate the poor and the weak with it. This is because in the pre-Islamic period, when they seized booty, the chief would take a quarter of it for himself, which was called *al-mirba'*, and then he would choose whatever he wished from it after the *mirba'*. Allah made this belong to His Messenger (ﷺ), to divide it as he was commanded. Then He said: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾, meaning what he gives you, ﴿gives you﴾ [from the *fay'* and the *ghanimah*] [[What is between the parentheses is missing from "a"]], ﴿take it, and whatever he forbids you﴾ from misappropriation and other things, ﴿refrain from it﴾. This was revealed concerning the wealth of *fay'*, but it is general for everything the Prophet (ﷺ) commanded and forbade.

Abd al-Wahid al-Malihi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Yusuf, Sufyan narrated to us, from Mansur, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from Abd Allah, who said: "Allah has cursed the women who tattoo and those who have themselves tattooed, the women who pluck their facial hair, and the women who file their teeth for beauty, who alter Allah's creation." News of this reached a woman from Banu Asad called Umm Ya'qub, so she came and said: "It has reached me that you cursed such-and-such." He said: "Why should I not curse one whom the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) cursed, and who is in the Book of Allah, the Exalted?" She said: "I have read everything between the two covers and did not find in it what you say." He said: "If you had read it, you would have found it. Did you not read: ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it, and whatever he forbids you, refrain from it﴾ [al-Hashr: 7]?" She said: "Yes." He said: "He has indeed forbidden it" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in *al-Tafsir*, surah al-Hashr, chapter on ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾: 8/630, and Muslim in *al-Libas*, chapter on the prohibition of the *wasilah* and the *mustawsilah* act, no. (2125): 3/1678.]]. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

Then he explained who has the right to the *fay'*, saying: ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their properties, seeking bounty﴾.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verse 8:

﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their wealth, seeking bounty﴾ (rizqan) ﴿from Allah and His good pleasure﴾. That is, they were driven out to the abode of emigration (Dar al-Hijrah), seeking the pleasure of Allah, Mighty and Majestic. ﴿And they help Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful ones﴾, in their faith.

Qatadah said: These are the emigrants who left their homes, their wealth, and their clans, and went out out of love for Allah and His Messenger, and chose Islam despite the hardship they were in. It has been related to us that a man would tie a stone around his belly to keep his spine upright from hunger, and a man would dig a pit in winter, having no covering other than it. [[Related by al-Tabari: 28/40. al-Suyuti also attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/105 to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Marwazi informed us; Abu al-Abbas al-Tahhan informed us; Abu Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Quraysh [[In manuscript B: Firas.]] ibn Sulayman informed us; Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Makki informed us; Abu Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam informed us: Abd al-Rahman ibn Mahdi related to me from Sufyan, from Abu Ishaq, from Umayyah ibn Khalid ibn Abd Allah ibn Usayd, from the Prophet ﷺ: that he used to begin (his supplication for victory) with the destitute emigrants (sa'alik al-muhajirin).

Abu Ubayd said: This is what Abd al-Rahman said, but in my opinion it is Umayyah ibn Abd Allah ibn Khalid ibn Usayd. [[Narrated by Abu Ubayd in Gharib al-Hadith: 1/248, al-Tabarani in al-Kabir: 1/269, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/264. Ibn Hajar mentioned it in al-Isabah: 1/246 from al-Tabarani's narration, and said: "This Umayyah has no companionship (sohbah) nor did he see the Prophet..." Al-Mundhiri also attributed it to al-Tabarani with the wording: "he used to begin with the destitute Muslims (sa'alik al-muslimin)," and said: "its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, but it is mursal." See al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib: 4/144. It is also mentioned in Mishkat al-Masabih (3/1444), attributed to Sharh al-Sunnah, and al-Albani declared it weak.]]

And we have related from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Rejoice, O group of destitute emigrants, with complete light on the Day of Resurrection; you will enter Paradise half a day before the wealthy people, and that is the equivalent of five hundred years." [[A weak hadith, narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Ilm, chapter on stories: 5/255-256, and Imam Ahmad: 3/63, 96. Al-Mundhiri said: its isnad contains al-Mu'alla ibn Ziyad Abu al-Hasan, about whom there is criticism. Al-Albani also mentioned it in Sahih al-Jami' under no. (40).]]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verse 9:**

﴿Those who had already settled in the abode and in faith﴾. The Ansar (Helpers) "settled in the abode" means they made the abode their home. That is, they took al-Madinah as the abode of the hijrah (emigration) and of faith. ﴿before them﴾ means they had embraced Islam in their own dwellings, had preferred faith, and had built the mosques two years before the Prophet ﷺ arrived.

The construction of the verse is: "And those who settled in the abode before them," that is, before the arrival of the emigrants (muhajirun) to them. They had believed, because faith is not a place that one settles in.

﴿They love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their hearts any need﴾, meaning any resentment (hazazah), anger (ghayz) or envy (hasad), ﴿of what they have been given﴾, meaning of the booty (fay') that was given to the emigrants instead of them. This is because the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divided the property of Banu al-Nadir among the emigrants and gave none of it to the Ansar, and the hearts of the Ansar were content with that. ﴿And they prefer them over themselves﴾, meaning they preferred their brothers among the emigrants over themselves, with their wealth and their homes. ﴿Even though they themselves were in need (khasasah)﴾, meaning poverty and need for what they gave up. This is because they shared their homes and their wealth with them.

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Musaddad narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Dawud narrated to us, from Fudayl ibn Ghazwan, from Abu Hazim, from Abu Hurayrah, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ and asked him for hospitality. He sent to his wives, "Do you have anything?" They said, "Nothing but water." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "Who will host this man?" A man from the Ansar said, "I will, O Messenger of Allah." He took him to his wife and said, "Honour the guest of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." She said, "We have nothing except the food of the children." He said, "Prepare your food, light your lamp, and put your children to sleep when they ask for supper." So she prepared her food, lit her lamp, and put her children to sleep. Then she got up as if to fix the lamp, and she extinguished it. The two of them then began to show him that they were eating, and they spent the night hungry. When the morning came, he went to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he said, "Allah laughed tonight (or he marvelled) at what you two did." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in Manaqib al-Ansar, chapter on the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: "And they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in need": 7/119, and Muslim in al-Ashribah, chapter on honouring the guest and its excellence, no. 2054: 3/1624.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, al-Hakam ibn Nafi' narrated to us, Shu'ayb informed us, Abu al-Zinad narrated to us, from al-A'raj, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Ansar said, "Divide the date palms between us and our brothers." He said, "No." They said, "Then let them take on the labour for us, and we will share the fruit with you." They said, "We hear and we obey" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Shurut, chapter on conditions in transactions: 5/322.]].

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Nu'aymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, who heard Anas ibn Malik when he went out with him to al-Walid, who said: The Prophet ﷺ invited the Ansar to grant them (the land of) Bahrayn. They said, "No, unless you grant our brothers among the emigrants the same." He said, "Be patient until you meet me at the Pool (al-hawd), for you will surely face favouritism (athrah) after me" [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Musaqah, chapter on land grants: 5/47, and in al-Jizyah wa al-Muwada'ah, chapter: what the Prophet ﷺ granted in Bahrayn...: 6/268.]].

It is related from Ibn Abbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to the Ansar on the day of al-Nadir: "If you wish, you may divide your wealth and your homes with the emigrants and share this spoil with them. And if you wish, your homes and your wealth will remain yours, and none of the spoil will be divided for you." The Ansar said, "Rather, we will share our wealth and our homes with them, and we will prefer them with the spoil, and we will not share in it." Then Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: "And they prefer them over themselves, even though they themselves were in need. And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul, those are the successful" [[See: al-Qurtubi: 18/25.]].

"Al-Shuhh" in the speech of the Arabs means stinginess (al-bukhl) and withholding of surplus. The scholars distinguished between shuhh and bukhl. It is reported that a man said to Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, "I fear that I may have perished." He said, "Why is that?" He said, "I hear Allah say: 'And whoever is protected from the stinginess of his soul...' and I am a stingy man, from whose hand almost nothing ever leaves." Abd Allah said, "That is not the shuhh that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned in the Qur'an. Rather, shuhh is that you devour the wealth of your brother unjustly, [159/a] and bukhl is the (ordinary) stinginess, and a bad thing is bukhl" [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/43. al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/107 also attributes it to Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, al-Firyabi, Sa'id ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab. al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/490. In its chain is al-Mas'udi, who is truthful but became confused before his death.]].

Ibn Umar said: Shuhh is not that a man withholds his wealth; rather, shuhh is that a man's eye longs for what is not his [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/107 to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Mardawayh.]]. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Shuhh" is taking what is forbidden and withholding zakat (obligatory alms) [[Attributed by al-Suyuti in al-Durr al-Manthur: 8/108 to Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir.]]. It has also been said: Shuhh is intense greed which drives a person to commit what is forbidden.

Ibn Zayd said: Whoever does not take what Allah has forbidden him, and whom shuhh does not drive to withhold anything of what Allah has commanded him to give, has indeed been protected from the stinginess of his soul [[Narrated by al-Tabari: 28/44.]].

Imam Abu Ali al-Husayn ibn Muhammad al-Qadi informed us, Abu Sa'd Khalaf ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nizar informed us, Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Hazzaz al-Qahandari narrated to us, Abu Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Ishaq al-Sa'di narrated to us, Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi narrated to us, al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, Dawud ibn Qays al-Farra' narrated to us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Miqsam, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. And beware of shuhh, for shuhh destroyed those who were before you; it drove them to shed their blood and to make lawful what was forbidden to them" [[Narrated by Muslim in al-Birr wa al-Silah wa al-Adab, chapter on the prohibition of injustice, no. 2578: 4/1996. The author also cites it in Sharh al-Sunnah: 14/357.]].

Ahmad ibn Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us, Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn Musa al-Sayrafi informed us, Abu al-Abbas al-Asamm narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Abd Allah ibn Abd al-Hakam informed us, my father and Shu'ayb informed us, both saying: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn al-Had, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from Safwan ibn Abi Yazid, from al-Qa'qa' (he is Ibn al-Lajlaj), from Abu Hurayrah, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "The dust of the path of Allah and the smoke of Hell never gather together in the belly of a servant, and shuhh and faith never gather together in the heart of a servant" [[Narrated by al-Nasa'i in al-Jihad, chapter on the excellence of one who works in the path of Allah with his feet: 6/13-14, and Ahmad: 2/256, 342, 441, and al-Hakim: 2/72, and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 10/354. See also Sahih al-Jami' (7616).]].

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 59, verses 10–11:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿And those who came after them﴾ means the Successors (al-Tabi'un), who are those who come after the Emigrants (al-Muhajirun) and the Helpers (al-Ansar), until the Day of Resurrection. Then He mentioned that they supplicate for themselves and for those who preceded them in faith and forgiveness, so He said: ﴿They say, "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not place in our hearts any resentment (ghill) toward those who have believed. Our Lord, indeed You are Kind and Merciful."﴾ Ghill means deceit, envy and hatred. Whoever has resentment in his heart toward any of the Companions (al-Sahabah) and does not ask Allah's mercy for all of them, then he is not among those whom Allah meant by this verse, because Allah, Exalted is He, arranged the believers into three ranks: the Emigrants, the Helpers, and the Successors who are described by what Allah mentioned. So whoever is not among the Successors with this description is outside the categories of the believers.

Ibn Abi Layla said: "People are of three ranks: the poor Emigrants, those who settled in the abode and in faith (al-Ansar), and those who came after them. So strive not to be outside these ranks." [[See: al-Tabari: 28 / 45.]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, Abdullah ibn Hamid informed us, Ahmad ibn Abdullah ibn Sulayman informed us, Ibn Numayr narrated to us, my father narrated to us from Isma'il ibn Ibrahim, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Masruq, from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "You were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of Muhammad (ﷺ), but you reviled them. I heard your Prophet (ﷺ) say: 'This Ummah will not perish until its last members curse its first.'" [[Narrated by Ibn Abi Shaybah in al-Musannaf: 15 / 125. Al-Haythami said in Majma' al-Zawa'id: 10 / 21: "Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Awsat, and in its chain is Isma'il ibn Ibrahim ibn Muhajir, who is weak. It is supported by what Muslim narrated in the Book of Tafsir from Urwah, who said: Aisha said to me: 'O nephew! They were commanded to seek forgiveness for the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ), but they reviled them.' Ibn Kathir also quoted it: 4 / 340, from al-Baghawi.]]

Malik ibn Mighwal said: Amir ibn Sharahil al-Sha'bi said: "O Malik, the Jews and the Christians are superior to the Rafidah in one quality [[In "A": bi-fadlah.]]. The Jews were asked: 'Who is the best of the people of your religion?' They said: 'The companions of Musa, peace be upon him.' The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if they help them, they will surely turn their backs.﴾ That is, even if their help were supposed to exist. Al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and Qur'an scholar) said: its meaning is that if they intended to help the Jews, they would turn their backs in defeat. ﴿Then they will not be helped.﴾ That is, the Banu al-Nadir will not become victorious when their helper is defeated.

﴿Indeed, you﴾ O assembly of Muslims ﴿are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah.﴾ That is, they fear you more than they fear Allah. ﴿That is﴾ that is, that fear of you ﴿because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾ the greatness of Allah.

﴿They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns﴾ meaning the Jews. That is, they will not come out to fight you; rather, they will fight you while sheltered by towns and walls. This is the words of Allah: ﴿or from behind walls.﴾ Ibn Kathir and Abu Amr recited "jidar" (in the singular). The others recited "judur" (in the plural), with a damma on the jim and a kasrah on the dal (dar).

﴿Their violence among themselves is severe.﴾ That is, some of them are harsh toward others, and their enmity toward one another is intense. It was said: their violence among themselves, behind the walls and fortresses, is severe; but when they come out against you, they are the most cowardly of Allah's creatures. ﴿You think them united, but their hearts are divided﴾ scattered and disunited. Qatadah said: the people of falsehood have divergent desires, divergent testimonies, and divergent deeds, yet they are united in enmity toward the people of truth. Mujahid said: it means that the religion of the hypocrites differs from the religion of the Jews.

﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾

﴿Like those before them of recent times, who tasted the consequence of their affair; and for them is a painful punishment (15). Like Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds" (16).﴾

﴿Like those before them﴾ meaning: the likeness of these Jews is like those before them ﴿of recent times﴾ meaning the polytheists of Makkah. ﴿Who tasted the consequence of their affair﴾ meaning the killing at Badr. This was before the expedition against the Banu al-Nadir, according to Mujahid. Ibn Abbas said: "like those before them" refers to the Banu Qaynuqa. It was also said: the likeness of Qurayzah is like that of the Banu al-Nadir, and there were two years between them.

﴿And for them is a painful punishment.﴾ Then He set forth an example for the hypocrites and the Jews together, regarding their forsaking [their allies] [[In manuscript "A": "tujadiluhum" (their disputing).]]. He said: ﴿Like Satan﴾ that is, the likeness of the hypocrites in their deceiving of the Banu al-Nadir and their abandoning them is like the likeness of Satan ﴿when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you."﴾

This is what 'Ata' and others narrated from Ibn Abbas, who said: There was a monk during the al-Fatrah (the interval between prophets) called "Barsisa," who worshipped in a hermitage (sawma'ah) for seventy years, during which he did not disobey Allah for the blink of an eye. Iblis was exhausted in devising schemes against him. So one day he gathered the rebellious devils and said: "Will none of you find someone to take care of Barsisa's affair for me?" Al-Abyad (he is the companion of the prophets, and he is the one who confronted the Prophet (ﷺ) and came to him in the form of Jibril in order to whisper to him in the guise of revelation, but Jibril pushed him to the farthest land of India) said: "I will take care of his affair." So he went, adorned himself with the adornments of monks, shaved the middle of his head, and came to Barsisa's hermitage and called out to him, but he did not respond. Barsisa would not turn from his prayer except once every ten days, and he would not break his fast except once every ten days.

When al-Abyad saw that he would not answer him, he devoted himself to worship at the base of Barsisa's hermitage. When Barsisa turned from his prayer, he looked out from his hermitage and saw al-Abyad standing in prayer in a fine manner of monastic appearance. When he saw this state of his, he regretted in himself that he had not answered him, and said to him: "You called out to me, and I was occupied with other things. What is your need?" He said: "My need is that I love to be with you, so that I may learn good conduct from you, take from your deeds and knowledge, and that we might gather in worship, so that you may supplicate for me and I may supplicate for you." Barsisa said: "I am busy with something other than you. If you are a believer, then Allah will grant you a share in what I supplicate for the believers, if He responds to me." Then he turned to his prayer and left al-Abyad. Al-Abyad began to pray, and Barsisa did not turn to him for forty days after that. When he finished, he saw him standing in prayer. When Barsisa saw the intensity of his striving, he said to him: "What is your need?" He said: "My need is that you permit me to ascend to you." He permitted him, and he ascended to him in his hermitage. He remained with him for a year, worshipping, not breaking his fast except once every forty days, and not turning from his prayer except once every forty days; sometimes he extended it to eighty. When Barsisa saw his striving, his own soul began to feel small in comparison, and the state of al-Abyad impressed him.

When the year had passed, al-Abyad said to Barsisa: "I am departing, for I have another companion besides you. I thought you were striving harder than what I see, and what reached us about you was other than what I have seen." That caused a severe distress to befall Barsisa, and he disliked parting from him because of what he had seen of his intense striving. When he bade him farewell, al-Abyad said to him: "I have supplications that I will teach you, which you may recite. They are better than what you are engaged in. Through them Allah cures the sick, and through them He restores health to the afflicted and the insane." Barsisa said: "I dislike this position, for I have a concern of my own, and I fear that if people learn of it, they will distract me from worship." Al-Abyad continued to press him until he taught him. Then he left and came to Iblis and said: "By Allah, I have ruined the man."

He said: Then al-Abyad went and waylaid a man and strangled him. Then he came in the form of a physician and said to his family: "Your companion has madness. Shall I treat him?" They said: "Yes." He said to them: "I am not able to overcome his possession, but I will direct you to one who supplicates to Allah, and He will cure him. Go to Barsisa, for with him is the Name which, when he supplicates with it, he is answered." So they went to him and asked him for this, and he supplicated with those words, and the devil departed from him. Al-Abyad would do the same to people, directing them to Barsisa, who would supplicate, and they would be healed.

Then al-Abyad went and waylaid a girl from among the daughters of the kings of the Children of Israel, who was among three brothers, and their father had been their king. He died and was succeeded by his brother, who became the king of the Children of Israel, and he was her paternal uncle. He tormented her and strangled her. Then he came to them in the form of a physician and said: "Do you want me to treat her?" They said: "Yes." He said: "The one who has seized her is a rebellious devil who cannot be overcome. But I will direct you to a man you trust. Leave her with him, and when her devil comes, he will supplicate for her until you know that she has been healed, and you may return her in good health." They said: "And who is he?" He said: "Barsisa." They said: "How can we get him to agree to this, when his station is greater than that?" He said: "Go and build a hermitage beside his hermitage, so that you may look down upon him. If he accepts her, well and good; otherwise, place her in her own hermitage, then say to him: 'She is a trust with you, so seek reward for her.'"

He said: They went to him and asked him, but he refused them. So they built a hermitage (ṣawmaʿa) according to what the white one (al-Abyaḍ) had instructed them, and they placed the girl in his hermitage, saying: "This is our sister, a trust (amānah), so seek reward for her (fa-ḥtasib fīhā)." Then they departed. When Barṣīṣā finished his prayer, he saw the girl and the beauty and loveliness that she had, and she fell into his heart, and a great matter entered upon him. Then he turned back to his prayer, and Satan came to her and strangled her, so Barṣīṣā invoked those supplications, and Satan departed from her. Then he turned to his prayer again, and Satan came to her and strangled her, so Barṣīṣā invoked those supplications. Then he turned to his prayer again, and Satan came to her and strangled her. She used to uncover herself to him, and Satan came to him and said: "Have intercourse with her, and afterwards you will repent, and you will attain what you desire of the matter." He did not cease to persuade him until he had intercourse with her. He continued in this manner, visiting her, until she became pregnant and her pregnancy became apparent. Then Satan said to him: "Woe to you, O Barṣīṣā, you have been exposed. Would you like to kill her and then repent? If they ask you, say: Her devil took her away, and I was unable to overcome him." So he entered and killed her, then he took her away and buried her beside the mountain. Satan came while he was burying her at night, and seized the edge of her garment, so an edge remained outside the dirt. Then Barṣīṣā returned to his hermitage and turned to his prayer, when her brothers came to check on their sister. They used to come at intervals of days, asking about her and entrusting her to him. They said: "O Barṣīṣā, what has happened to our sister?" He said: "Her devil came and took her away, and I could not withstand him." They believed him and departed. When evening came and they were distressed, Satan came to the eldest of them in his sleep and said: "Woe to you! Barṣīṣā did such and such to your sister, and he buried her in such and such a place." The brother said to himself: "This is a dream, and it is from the work of Satan, for Barṣīṣā is better than that." He said: So it was repeated to him for three nights, and he paid it no heed. Then he went to the middle one with the same, and the middle one said what the eldest had said, and he told no one. Then he went to the youngest with the same, and the youngest said to his two brothers: "By God, I saw such and such." The middle one said: "By God, I too have seen the same." The eldest said: "I too saw the same." So they went to Barṣīṣā and said: "O Barṣīṣā, what has happened to our sister?" He said: "Did I not inform you of her condition? Do you accuse me?" They said: "By God, we do not accuse you," and they were ashamed before him, and they departed. Then Satan came to them and said: "Woe to you! She is indeed buried in such and such a place, and the edge of her garment is outside the dirt." So they went and found their sister in the state they had seen in the dream. They walked with their clients (mawālī) and their servants, carrying axes and shovels, and they demolished his hermitage and brought him down. Then they bound him and took him to the king, and he confessed against himself. That was because Satan came to him and said: "You kill her and then deny it? Two matters will be gathered against you: killing and denial. Confess." When he confessed, the king ordered his execution and crucifixion upon a piece of wood. When he was crucified, al-Abyaḍ came to him and said: "O Barṣīṣā, do you know me?" He said: "No." He said: "I am your companion who taught you the supplications, so that you were answered. Woe to you! Did you not fear God regarding your trust? You betrayed its people, and you claimed that you were the most devout of the Children of Israel. Were you not ashamed?" He continued to reproach him. Then at the end of that he said: "Has what you did not sufficed you, until you confessed against yourself, disgraced yourself, and disgraced your likes among the people? If you die in this state, none of your peers will prosper." He said: "What shall I do?" He said: "Obey me in one matter, so that I may save you from what you are in: I will take hold of their eyes and bring you out from your place!" He said: "And what is it?" He said: "You prostrate to me." He said: "I cannot." He said: "Do it." [What is between the brackets is omitted from manuscript "A".] So he prostrated to him, and he said: "O Barṣīṣā, this is what I wanted from you. The outcome of your affair has become that you disbelieved in your Lord. Indeed I am free of you." "Indeed I fear God, Lord of the worlds." [Al-Ṭabarī narrated it in abridged form: 28/50, and al-Suyūṭī attributed it in al-Durr al-Manthūr: 8/117 to Ibn Abī Ḥātim, abridging al-Ṭabarī. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verses 12–16 (part 1 of 2):

﴿Whether they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and whether they are fought, they will not help them.﴾ The matter was as Allah stated. They were expelled from their homes, and the hypocrites did not go out with them. They were fought, and the hypocrites did not help them. The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if they help them, they will surely turn their backs.﴾ That is, even if their help were supposed to exist. Al-Zajjaj (a grammarian and Qur'an scholar) said: its meaning is that if they intended to help the Jews, they would turn their backs in defeat. ﴿Then they will not be helped.﴾ That is, the Banu al-Nadir will not become victorious when their helper is defeated.

﴿Indeed, you﴾ O assembly of Muslims ﴿are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah.﴾ That is, they fear you more than they fear Allah. ﴿That is﴾ that is, that fear of you ﴿because they are a people who do not comprehend﴾ the greatness of Allah.

﴿They will not fight you all together except within fortified towns﴾ meaning the Jews. That is, they will not come out to fight you; rather, they will fight you while sheltered by towns and walls. The others recited "judur" (in the plural), with a damma on the jim and a kasrah on the dal (dar).

﴿That is because they are a people who do not reason.﴾

﴿Like those before them of recent times, who tasted the consequence of their affair; and for them is a painful punishment (15). Like Satan when he says to man, "Disbelieve." And when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds" (16).﴾

It was also said: the likeness of Qurayzah is like that of the Banu al-Nadir, and there were two years between them.

Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil*, on surah 59, verse 17:

Allah the Exalted says, ﴿So the outcome of both of them was that they would be in the Fire, abiding therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾ He means Satan and that man.

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah struck this parable for the Jews of Banu al-Nadir and the hypocrites of Madinah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, had commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to expel Banu al-Nadir from Madinah. The hypocrites sent secret messages to them, saying: "Do not respond to Muhammad in what he calls you to, and do not leave your homes. If he fights you, we are with you; and if he expels you, we will go out with you." They accepted this, so they fortified their strongholds and barricaded themselves in their homes, hoping for the support of the hypocrites. Then the Prophet (ﷺ) came to them, and they took up arms against him, hoping for the hypocrites' support. But the hypocrites abandoned them and disowned them, just as Satan disowned Barsisa and abandoned him. So the outcome for both groups was the Fire.

Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with him) said: After that, the monks among the Children of Israel did not walk about except in *taqiyyah* (concealment of their faith out of caution) and secrecy. The people of wickedness and immorality became bold against the rabbis (*ahbar*, the Jewish scholars), and they accused them with slander and foul things, until there came the matter of Juraij the monk. When Allah cleared him of what they had accused him of, the monks became free after him and appeared openly to the people.

The story of Juraij is as follows, as was related to us by Isma'il ibn 'Abd al-Qahir: 'Abd al-Ghafir ibn Muhammad informed us: Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Juludi narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Sufyan narrated to us: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj narrated to us: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us: Jarir ibn Hazim informed us: Muhammad ibn Sirin narrated to us, from Abu Hurairah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Only three spoke in the cradle: 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him), the companion of Juraij, and Juraij was a worshipper who took for himself a hermitage (*sawma'ah*) and stayed in it. His mother came to him while he was praying and said, 'O Juraij!' He said, 'O Lord, my mother and my prayer!' So he continued with his prayer. She went away, and the next day she came to him while he was praying and said, 'O Juraij!' He said, 'O Lord, my mother and my prayer!' So he continued with his prayer. She said, 'O Allah, do not let him die until he looks upon the faces of prostitutes.'"

The Children of Israel spoke of Juraij and his worship. There was a prostitute (*baghiyy*) whose beauty was famous, and she said, "If you wish, I will tempt him for you." He said: So she presented herself to him, but he did not turn to her. She then went to a shepherd who used to take shelter near his hermitage, and she gave herself to him. He had intercourse with her, and she became pregnant. When she gave birth, she said, "It is from Juraij." So they came to him, brought him down from his hermitage, demolished his hermitage, and began to beat him. He said, "What is the matter with you?" They said, "You committed fornication with this prostitute, and she has borne a child by you." He said, "Where is the child?" They brought the child, and he said, "Leave me until I have prayed." He prayed, and when he had finished, he came to the child, prodded his belly, and said, "O boy, who is your father?" The child said, "So-and-so the shepherd." They then turned to Juraij, kissing him and seeking blessing from him, and said, "We will build your hermitage for you of gold." He said, "No, rebuild it of clay as it was." So they did.

While a child was nursing from his mother, a man riding a fine mount and of handsome appearance passed by. His mother said, "O Allah, make my son like this man." So the child left the breast, turned to look at him, and said, "O Allah, do not make me like him." Then he returned to his breast and began to nurse. He (the narrator) said: "It is as if I were looking at the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) as he imitated the child's nursing by putting his index finger in his mouth and sucking it."

He said: They also passed by a slave girl whom they were beating, saying, "You have committed fornication and theft," while she said, "Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs." The child's mother said, "O Allah, do not make my son like her." So the child left off nursing, looked at her, and said, "O Allah, make me like her." At that, they (the mother and the child) argued about the matter. She said, "A man of good appearance passed by, and I said, 'O Allah, make my son like him,' and you said, 'O Allah, do not make me like him.' They passed by this slave girl, whom they were beating and saying, 'You have committed fornication and theft,' and I said, 'O Allah, do not make my son like her,' and you said, 'O Allah, make me like her.'" He said: "That man was a tyrant, so I said, 'O Allah, do not make me like him.' As for this girl, they say to her, 'You have committed fornication,' when she has not, and 'You have stolen,' when she has not, so I said, 'O Allah, make me like her.'"

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 59, verse 24:**

﴿He is Allah, the Creator﴾ (al-Khaliq), the one who decrees and who transforms a thing through management from one state to another, as He said: "He creates you in the wombs of your mothers, creation after creation" [al-Zumar: 6]. ﴿The Originator﴾ (al-Bari'), the one who brings existing things into being from non-existence to existence. ﴿The Fashioner﴾ (al-Musawwir), the one who gives forms to created beings through the marks by which some of them are distinguished from others. It is said: "This is the form (surah) of the matter," meaning its example. Thus first comes creation (khalq), then origination (bara'), then shaping (taswir).

﴿To Him belong the Most Beautiful Names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise﴾.

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us: Ibn Fanjawayh informed me: Ibn Shayba related to us: Ibn Wahb related to us: Ahmad ibn Abi Shurayh and Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ramadi related to us, both saying: Abu Ahmad al-Zubayri informed us: Khalid ibn Tahman related to us: Nafi' ibn Abi Nafi' related to me, from Ma'qil ibn Yasar, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says, when he wakes in the morning, three times, 'I seek refuge in Allah, the All-Hearing, the All-Knowing, from the accursed Satan,' and recites the last three verses of Surat al-Hashr, Allah will appoint seventy thousand angels to ask forgiveness for him until evening. If he dies that day, he dies as a martyr. And whoever says it when he enters the evening will have the same station."
